name: Android Green
lede: Android Green is the bright, yellowish green of Google's Android robot logo.

sections.title: A tech brand's green
sections.body: The name is a brand override: ColorHub's library notes it as the Android logo green, with Wikipedia citing Google as the source [1]. It has no earlier pigment, dye or dictionary history; it exists because a software platform's mascot was drawn in this exact shade [1]. The nearest named look-alikes are [[android-green]] and [[aqua-green]], with [[malachite]] and [[seaweed]] a little further off [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: No painting in our 23,781-painting archive holds this green covering at least one percent of its canvas, as photographed [3]. That is expected: it is a recent screen color built for a logo, not a pigment that painters ever mixed [3]. It joins a growing set of brand and interface colors, like many app-icon greens, that exist only as screen values with no pigment or dye history behind them [3]. Screen greens built for logos rarely find their way onto a painter's palette at all [3].

questions.q: Android Green is named for what?
True or false: Android Green has a pigment or dye history predating the Android logo.

openers: Android Green has no pigment history; it was built for a phone logo.
